summary.short: Directs the Federal Trade Commission to issue regulations requiring covered entities that provide use of or services from foundation models to disclose information about training data, documentation, testing and operations, and to submit specified information to the Commission. Regulations apply 90 days after promulgation.
summary.long: The bill directs the Federal Trade Commission, within one year of enactment and in consultation with NIST, Commerce and OSTP, to issue regulations requiring covered entities to publish and submit information about foundation models. Required content includes training data sources, collection and composition, data governance, intended uses and foreseeable risks, version and knowledge cutoff, supported languages, alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, benchmark performance, and computational power used. Covered entities are persons providing use of or services from a foundation model that meet any of four tests: high-capability performance on risky tasks, over 10,000,000 aggregate monthly users, over 10,000,000 monthly downloads, or training compute above 10^26 operations. Fully open-source models are exempt. Publication in a system or model card can count as compliance, and redactions are allowed for cybersecurity, public safety, national security or compliance with federal law if identified and justified. Derivative models must link to the base model's disclosure page and comply with rules for significant changes. Small and new businesses receive compliance guidance and a three-month grace period from penalties. Violations are treated as violations of an FTC rule on unfair or deceptive practices, with enforcement after 14 days' notice. The regulations apply 90 days after promulgation and are reviewed annually.

notes: Standalone bill: it creates new FTC rulemaking and does not amend, repeal or implement an existing instrument; only statutory cross-references are listed. Internal inconsistency: Sec. 2(l)(3)(B) lets the Commission update the number of monthly output instances for subparagraph (A)(i), but (A)(i) contains no output-instance figure. Sec. 2(d) is headed 'Consideration of Alternative Provisions' while its operative text says the Commission 'shall require' downstream models to comply. The term 'fully open-source model' in Sec. 2(c) is not defined. Sec. 2(j)(2)(A) is qualified by 'Except as provided in subsection (l)(3)(C)', which only defines covered persons. Text is the introduced version (IH) of 26 March 2026.
